Description: One of the oldest nearly complete Bibles in the world, written in Greek in the fourth century and first recorded in a Vatican Library catalogue in 1475; its earlier history is unknown. It contains most of the Old and New Testaments and is, with Sinaiticus, one of the two pillars of modern New Testament scholarship.
BiblicalSignificance: For centuries this manuscript sat in the Vatican's library while the church read the Bible in Latin translation — and when scholars finally compared it with the received text, it confirmed how carefully the Greek New Testament had been preserved. Two fourth-century Bibles, kept a thousand miles apart, agree with each other and with the Bibles in our hands.
